concepts.name: Atomic structure and subatomic particles
concepts.summary: Recall that atoms consist of a nucleus of protons and neutrons surrounded by electrons, and state each particle's charge and relative mass.

concepts.name: Atomic number and mass number
concepts.summary: Explain how atomic number defines an element and how mass number and neutron count give isotopes.

concepts.name: Periodic table organization
concepts.summary: Describe how elements are arranged in periods and groups and locate metals, nonmetals, and metalloids.

concepts.name: Elements, compounds, and mixtures
concepts.summary: Distinguish elements, compounds, and homogeneous and heterogeneous mixtures by composition.

concepts.name: Chemical formulas and symbols
concepts.summary: Read chemical symbols and formulas to state which elements and how many atoms are present.

concepts.name: Physical versus chemical change
concepts.summary: Classify changes as physical or chemical and identify evidence that a new substance has formed.

concepts.name: States of matter and particle model
concepts.summary: Describe solids, liquids, and gases in terms of particle arrangement and motion and name the phase changes.

misconceptions.text: Atoms of the same element always have the same number of neutrons.
Dissolving or changing state creates a new substance, so it is a chemical change.
A compound is just a mixture of elements that can be separated by physical means.

concepts.name: Electron configuration and valence electrons
concepts.summary: Write electron configurations for light elements and determine valence electrons from group position.

concepts.name: Ionic and covalent bonding
concepts.summary: Explain bond formation by electron transfer versus sharing and predict which type forms between given elements.

concepts.name: Naming compounds and writing formulas
concepts.summary: Apply naming rules to ionic and simple molecular compounds and derive formulas from ion charges.

concepts.name: Balancing chemical equations
concepts.summary: Balance equations by adjusting coefficients so each element's atoms are conserved.

concepts.name: Molar mass and the mole
concepts.summary: Convert between mass, moles, and number of particles using molar mass and Avogadro's number.

concepts.name: Periodic trends
concepts.summary: Use group and period position to predict trends in atomic radius, ionization energy, and electronegativity.

concepts.name: Reaction types
concepts.summary: Classify reactions as synthesis, decomposition, single or double replacement, or combustion and predict simple products.

misconceptions.text: Changing subscripts in a formula is an acceptable way to balance an equation.
A mole is a fixed mass of 6.022×10^23 grams of any substance.
Ionic compounds exist as discrete molecules like covalent ones.

concepts.name: Mole-ratio stoichiometry
concepts.summary: Use balanced-equation coefficients to convert between masses, moles, volumes, and particle counts of reactants and products.

concepts.name: Limiting reagent and percent yield
concepts.summary: Identify the limiting reactant from given quantities and calculate theoretical and percent yield.

concepts.name: Lewis structures and VSEPR geometry
concepts.summary: Draw Lewis structures and use electron-domain repulsion to predict shape and bond angles.

concepts.name: Molecular polarity and intermolecular forces
concepts.summary: Analyse bond polarity and geometry to determine molecular polarity and the dominant intermolecular forces.

concepts.name: Gas laws and ideal gas equation
concepts.summary: Apply Boyle's, Charles's, and the ideal gas law to relate pressure, volume, temperature, and moles.

concepts.name: Solution concentration and dilution
concepts.summary: Calculate molarity and use dilution relationships to prepare and analyse solutions.

concepts.name: Enthalpy and calorimetry
concepts.summary: Calculate heat transfer with q = mcΔT and interpret exothermic and endothermic enthalpy changes.

concepts.name: Acid-base definitions and pH
concepts.summary: Apply Arrhenius and Brønsted-Lowry definitions and calculate pH and pOH of strong acids and bases.

misconceptions.text: The limiting reagent is the reactant present in the smallest mass.
Molecules with polar bonds are always polar molecules.
Temperature in gas law calculations can be used in Celsius.

concepts.name: Chemical equilibrium and Le Chatelier
concepts.summary: Write equilibrium expressions, use K and Q to predict direction, and analyse how stresses shift equilibrium.

concepts.name: Weak acid-base equilibria and buffers
concepts.summary: Calculate pH for weak acids and bases using Ka and Kb and explain how buffers resist pH change.

concepts.name: Titration curves and indicators
concepts.summary: Interpret titration curves to locate equivalence points and choose suitable indicators.

concepts.name: Reaction kinetics and rate laws
concepts.summary: Determine rate laws from experimental data and relate rate to concentration, temperature, and activation energy.

concepts.name: Hess's law and thermochemical cycles
concepts.summary: Combine reaction enthalpies and formation data to find unknown enthalpy changes.

concepts.name: Thermodynamics and spontaneity
concepts.summary: Evaluate spontaneity using ΔG = ΔH − TΔS and relate ΔG to the equilibrium constant.

concepts.name: Solubility equilibria
concepts.summary: Use Ksp to evaluate solubility, precipitation, and the common-ion effect.

concepts.name: Redox reactions and electrochemistry
concepts.summary: Balance redox equations and analyse cell potentials in galvanic cells.

misconceptions.text: At equilibrium, reactions have stopped and concentrations of reactants and products are equal.
Exothermic reactions are always spontaneous, and a catalyst changes the equilibrium position.
A larger Ksp always means a more soluble salt regardless of formula stoichiometry.

concepts.name: Quantum model and orbital theory
concepts.summary: Evaluate how orbitals, hybridization, and molecular orbital theory explain bonding, magnetism, and exceptions to simple models.

concepts.name: Mechanistic analysis of kinetics
concepts.summary: Judge proposed mechanisms against rate laws using rate-determining steps and intermediates.

concepts.name: Statistical basis of entropy
concepts.summary: Explain entropy and free energy through microstates and energy dispersal, and evaluate their predictions across systems.

concepts.name: Nonideal solutions and colligative properties
concepts.summary: Evaluate deviations from ideal behaviour in solutions and gases and use colligative properties to determine molar mass.

concepts.name: Nernst equation and cell thermodynamics
concepts.summary: Connect cell potential, ΔG, and K, and predict potentials under nonstandard conditions.

concepts.name: Experimental design and error analysis
concepts.summary: Design quantitative experiments, propagate uncertainties, and critique methods and conclusions.

concepts.name: Multi-equilibria system modelling
concepts.summary: Construct models of systems with coupled acid-base, solubility, and complexation equilibria and justify approximations.

misconceptions.text: Lewis structures and VSEPR accurately describe all bonding, including delocalized and paramagnetic species.
Entropy simply means disorder, so any increase in apparent messiness means spontaneity.
Ideal-solution and dilute-approximation equations hold accurately at any concentration.
